body.statement: For every \(I\in\mathfrak J_q^{\mathrm{nw}}\), each local feasible set is the nonempty bounded real polyhedron \(K_c=\{z_c\in\mathbb R^{R_c}:H_cz_c\le h_c\}\), with \(H_c=[A_c^{\mathsf T},-A_c^{\mathsf T},-I_{R_c}]^{\mathsf T}\) and \(h_c=[b_c^{\mathsf T},-b_c^{\mathsf T},0^{\mathsf T}]^{\mathsf T}\). Each equality factor is the nonempty bounded real polyhedron \(K_H=\{x_H\in\mathbb R^H:H_Hx_H\le h_H\}\) with the analogous explicit rational matrices. For a fixed external-parent context, summing the partition rows supported in \(H\) gives \(\sum_{r\in H}x_{H,r}=\mu_H\) for a rational \(0\le\mu_H\le1\); hence every \(K_c\) and \(K_H\) is closed, bounded, and compact. If also \(I\in\mathfrak J_{q,k}\), then \(|H|\le q^2(k+1)\).
body.justification: The feasible objects must be genuine compact subsets of finite-dimensional real spaces before compactness or vertex arguments can be invoked.
body.gap: The canonical causal-program papers write equality-and-nonnegativity systems, but do not isolate the within-block factors with this explicit H-representation and factorwise mass bound.
body.consumer: Every later use of compactness and finite support domains is grounded in an auditable rational inequality system.
